One Stop Systems on FTSE Russell's preliminary Russell 3000 deletion list
news.summary: OSS appears on the preliminary deletion list for FTSE Russell's first semi-annual December reconstitution, meaning it would leave the Russell 3000 and Russell 2000 only six months after joining in June. Changes take effect after the close on December 11, which typically brings forced index-fund selling around that date.

news.headline: OSS Receives 10th Order Since May 2025 from Leading Defense and Intelligence Contractor
news.summary: One Stop Systems reported its tenth follow-on order since May 2025 from an unnamed defense and intelligence prime contractor for its rugged edge-compute hardware. The repeat business, three days after a $2.75M U.S. Army development award, supports the company's push to grow its defense segment; the order value was not stated in the headline coverage.

news.headline: OSS Awarded $2.75 Million Contract by U.S. Army to Develop Next-Generation Compute Appliance for Tactical Ground Vehicles
news.summary: The U.S. Army awarded OSS a $2.75M contract to develop a next-generation compute appliance for tactical ground vehicles. It extends OSS's existing rugged-edge work for Army vehicle programs and adds to its defense pipeline.

news.headline: Lake Street Maintains Buy on One Stop Systems, Cuts Target to $15
news.summary: Lake Street kept its Buy rating after Q3 but lowered its price target to $15. Like A.G.P., it pointed to lower valuation multiples and near-term margin pressure.

news.headline: One Stop Systems Reports Q3 2026 Results
news.summary: Continuing-operations revenue rose about 36% to $12.6M, with year-to-date book-to-bill of 1.46. Full-year growth guidance was raised to about 40%, but a bad-debt charge and a legal settlement deepened the quarterly loss.

news.headline: One Stop Systems Launches $50M At-The-Market Equity Offering With Piper Sandler
news.summary: OSS signed an equity distribution agreement letting it sell up to $50M of common stock over time through Piper Sandler. This adds potential dilution, and the stock slid after the release.

catalysts.label: Russell 3000/2000 deletion takes effect
catalysts.detail: Preliminary list (Nov 13) shows OSS exiting the Russell 3000 in the December 2026 reconstitution; changes are effective after the close on Dec 11, with reconstituted indexes trading from Dec 14. Expect index-fund selling pressure into that close; lists are final once FTSE Russell locks them in early December.

catalysts.label: Q4/FY2026 results
catalysts.detail: Expected around March 2027; date not announced. Watch whether ~40% FY growth guidance is met and whether the ATM is used.

pulse: OSS has followed its Q3 report with a string of defense wins: a $2.75M U.S. Army contract on Nov 9 to develop a next-generation tactical-vehicle compute appliance and, on Nov 12, a follow-on production order from a defense and intelligence contractor, its 10th since May 2025. Q3 revenue grew about 36% to $12.6M and FY2026 growth guidance was raised to ~40%, but the stock remains well below summer levels after the post-Q3 selloff on margin strain, one-off charges and a new $50M ATM; analysts keep Buy ratings with trimmed targets (A.G.P. $16, Lake Street and Roth $15). A new headwind: OSS is on the preliminary list to leave the Russell 3000/2000 in the December reconstitution (effective after the close on Dec 11), which usually means index-fund selling; Q4 results around March 2027 are the next fundamental test.
